$comment: Operating assumptions. Freight, shrink and handling are the real cost of doing business in Indian F&V retail; a margin tool that only compares mandi price to retail price is a toy, because the two are never the whole cost.

costs.freightNote: 62 km PC to dark store, then last mile, amortised over 5,000 kg/day
costs.handlingNote: Grading, sorting, palletising at the PC
costs.coldChainNote: Applied to chilled lines only; set coldChainRequired per commodity
costs.shrinkNote: Modelled shrinkage from grade-out plus transit loss. Expressed as a share of the *purchased* weight, so it is charged before margin, not after.

margin.$note: A sub-target margin is a warning; a negative one is a breach. Fill rate is tracked separately because a thin-margin line sold at a high rate can be more profitable than a fat-margin line that does not sell.

thresholds.priceSpikeNote: Day-on-day mandi move that triggers a PRICE_SPIKE flag
thresholds.priceCollapseNote: Day-on-day fall that triggers an opportunity flag -- cheap stock is worth taking if the shrink holds
thresholds.costToRetailNote: The breach ceiling, EXPRESSED AS A MARGIN BUFFER rather than picked directly. 100 - (target 22% - buffer 6%) = 84%. These two settings must stay coherent: a hardcoded cost-to-retail ceiling can silently contradict the margin target, and a line that merely sits below target would then be reported as a breach rather than a watch. At 84% the line is 6pp under target, which is a real problem, not a rounding difference. Set the buffer to 0 for a strictly literal breach.
thresholds.daysBelowTargetNote: Consecutive days below target margin before escalating to REVIEW

sim.shockNote: Daily probability of a supply or weather shock. This is what makes the simulation interesting: F&V mandi rates do not random-walk politely, they jump.
